ideas.title: The sketch
ideas.note: Build a layered digital twin — cell, then organ, then whole body — trained on multi-omic and clinical data, so experiments can run in silico first: perturb a pathway, dose a virtual liver, and watch the effect propagate upward through the layers. Wet-lab time then goes only to the candidates that survive simulation, and every real result feeds back to sharpen the twin. The statistics is the hard part, and the interesting part: calibration, uncertainty, and knowing exactly when the simulation deserves to be trusted.

topic: A Self-Evolving AI for Automated Signal Discovery

ideas.title: The sketch
ideas.note: A closed loop where AI does the whole job: propose a hypothesis, run the analysis, judge the evidence, refine the question — do, learn, refine, again and again through the night, with humans auditing the trail instead of driving every step. The open problem is honesty at machine scale: multiplicity control and calibrated skepticism, so a system that tests a million hypotheses can't fool itself — or us.
